text:
Alex Kim: thinking out loud — proposal to break the main enqueue into adaptive "queue strata" (fast, medium, slow) instead of a single continuous batcher. goal: reduce SLO misses for tiny interactive requests without losing packing efficiency for bulk traffic.
Priya Shah: curious — how do you see admission working? token affinity still preserved?
Alex Kim: admission would pick a strata based on a cost/latency hint + recent per-tenant tail. token affinity stays inside a strata; cross-strata KV cache access is read-through but writeback gated.
Marco Ruiz: my worry is fragmentation. if we split lanes we might create many half-full batches and regress cost. any packing mitigation ideas?
Linh Tran: maybe add a dynamic bleed where slow strata can donate unused headroom to fast strata for a short window. keeps efficient packing but prioritizes latency.
Samira Gomez: sounds promising. need concrete contract for that donation — how long, how to revoke? also telemetry to prove it's helping.
Alex Kim: basic sketch for donation policy: max_donation_ms, donor_threshold_pct, preemptible_token_count. short example config: ```donation: { max_donation_ms: 20, donor_threshold_pct: 0.6, preemptible_token_count: 8 }```
Priya Shah: how do we handle eviction and KV cache warmup when a tenant hops between strata? cold KVs will cause tail spikes.
Marco Ruiz: we can maintain per-tenant warmup credit; when a tenant moves up to fast strata we reserve a tiny prefetch budget to warm KV cache. charge it back as part of billing metrics.
Linh Tran: observability: emit span tags: strata, donated_ms, prefetch_tokens, kv_warm_hit_rate. need percentile breakdowns by tenant and by model.
Samira Gomez: ops question — if fast lane saturates, do we autoscale it separately? or just degrade tenants into medium?
Alex Kim: idea: two-tier autoscale. fast lane scales aggressively for CPU/GPU slices that benefit latency; medium/slow scale more for throughput. Also implement graceful degradation: overflow policy = { prefer_medium, then slow }
Priya Shah: edge case: a single tenant sends bursts that abuse donation and starve other fast tenants. mitigation?
Marco Ruiz: enforce per-tenant donation caps + fairness window. plus a circuit breaker that prevents repeated donations above threshold.
Linh Tran: for rollout, suggest feature-flagged path with metric gates: p50/p95 latency by strata, packing efficiency, token-per-second cost delta. if packing cost > 5% revert.
Samira Gomez: +1. also add runbook: how to revert donation and force coalescing back into single batcher. keep a safe default toggle.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: created feature flag `adaptive-queue-strata-v1`, added canary on 10% of hosts, log level TRACE for strata selector for 24h.
Alex Kim: next steps: implement selector + donation proto in a small prototype, add observability fields Linh listed, and run a 48h canary. volunteer: Marco for selector, Priya for cache warmup, Linh for dashboards.
Priya Shah: I can mock the warmup budget and validate with replay traces.
Marco Ruiz: I'll start on selector sketch tomorrow. I'll post a short PR and perf baseline numbers.
Linh Tran: I'll wire up dashboards and a quick eval job to replay 1M requests.
Samira Gomez: adding runbook draft to runbook repo after canary. will include escalation steps. :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: cool — capturing action items. if anyone thinks of simpler option (e.g., soft-priority + single batcher) speak now, otherwise prototype time.
Marco Ruiz: one more thought — test with quantized models where KV prefetch costs differ. that might change donation thresholds.
Alex Kim: good call. include model heterogeneity in canary matrix.
Samira Gomez: noted. I'll add a checklist item.
Alex Kim: thanks all — let's keep updates in this thread.
